hypotheses.content: Donor-free aromatic and hydrophobic graphs have topology- and packing-dependent residuals beyond size and LogP.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Topology and heavy-atom anchors can improve transfer among common donor-free aromatic rows where descriptor similarity alone leaves residual error.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do matched topology and heavy-atom contrasts reduce residuals after PE/EA and loading are controlled?

hypotheses.content: Oxygenated and carbonyl-rich graphs often require endpoint-specific V2-tail corrections, with effects depending on topology and condition.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched oxygenated and carbonyl points can teach when V2 broadening is structural rather than a uniform late-retention offset.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which carbonyl, donor, fused-graph, and loading combinations generate V2 tails independently of V1?

hypotheses.content: Aromatic-basic and amino-nitrile structures require graph-conditioned transfer; nitrogen environments do not share one correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Graph-specific nitrogen anchors can prevent a blanket acceptor-count or aromaticity correction from degrading generalization.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Can the retrained graph model separate nitrogen accessibility, basicity, and positional environment from formal acceptor count?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount and sparse heteroatom environments can alter V1 and V2 differently, with family-specific effects.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Loading contrasts and rare heteroatom anchors can teach separate onset and completion responses while repairing extrapolation into uncovered chemical regions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Within each graph family, does loading mainly shift onset, broaden completion, or alter both with PE/EA?

feedback_interpretation: Recent outcomes weakened any universal late-retention or V2-tail correction. Several oxygenated rows showed strong V2 overprediction, while other carbonyl and oxygen-rich rows had large measured late tails; common donor-free anchors were often closer. The persistent severe region is aromatic nitrogen, especially fused or basic graphs and amino-nitrile positional isomers. This batch therefore emphasizes matched condition curves and loading contrasts in carbonyl, oxygenated, nitrile, amino ester, and donor-free topology families, with sparse heteroatom anchors for extrapolation repair.
batch_rationale: The batch contains repeated graphs at different PE/EA ratios or loadings, allowing the retrained model to distinguish structural offsets from condition slopes and to learn separate V1 and V2 loading effects. Fused donor-free, nitrile, carbonyl, ester, alcohol, and sulfur-containing rows extend coverage across graph environments represented in the Row-distribution. Broad-width and high-CW candidates target likely transfer failures, while compact common-family anchors support interpolation. These complementary labels should improve generalization without relying on a single universal polarity or late-retention correction.
